visual.general_description: Six grayscale chest CT images in a 3-row by 2-column grid: an axial slice on the left and a coronal reformat on the right at each of three levels, overlaid with red block arrows.
visual.detailed_description: Each row pairs an axial lung-window image (left, dark circular field of view) with a coronal reformat (right). A thin orange horizontal reference line crosses each of the three axial images. Bright red block arrows are overlaid, two per image: row 1 axial arrows at the outer edge of one lung and at the upper margin of the other lung; row 1 coronal arrows at the upper zone of one lung (pointing down) and the outer margin of the other lung (pointing left); row 2 axial and coronal arrows at the lateral/lower margins of both lungs; row 3 axial arrows at the posterior-lateral lung bases and row 3 coronal arrows over both lower lung zones. Both lungs show widespread patchy ground-glass haze with scattered small nodular opacities and reticular lines in rows 1-2; the lower zones in row 3 show denser, more confluent opacification with speckled aerated lucencies, more prominent in the coronal view. The heart and mediastinal vessels appear bright white. Small bright dots and thin curvilinear lines lie outside the chest wall in some axial images, and tiny illegible scanner text appears along the left image margins. No lettered panels, patient identifiers or legible measurements are visible.
